hypothesis: Which profilers work inside the P1 Lambda (python3.12, arm64, 10,240 MB, SnapStart) and what each costs. Each profiler arm runs P1's code with one profiler on; its cost is the difference in Lambda's own REPORT numbers against a REPORT-only control (rep), paired by round (and by request for warm), CPU part 0xd40 rows only, judged against rep2, a second byte-identical REPORT-only function run in the same rounds, as a paired null. 'nvidia-spi' (the operator's word) is read as NVIDIA's tooling: nvidia-smi and Nsight Systems/Compute.

changed_variable.name: profiler
changed_variable.experiment: one of: P1 phase timers (none), cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, lkaisamp native sampler, X-Ray active tracing, Telemetry API extension

conclusion: Applicability (in Lambda): NVIDIA tools (nvidia-smi, nsys, ncu) are INAPPLICABLE because there is no GPU (no /dev/nvidia*, no PCI 0x10de, no driver or libraries; 7 probe environments, all CPU part 0xd40). perf, eBPF, ptrace and py-spy --native are DENIED (EPERM; CapEff 0, seccomp filter, perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU). These WORK: P1 phase timers, REPORT/CloudWatch, X-Ray, the Telemetry API extension, cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, and an in-process SIGPROF sampler (lkaisamp), which gives native KleidiAI kernel profiles where perf is denied. Overhead (run 20261020T231634Z: 8 arms, 4,800 invocations, 0 errors, a fresh Lambda client per wave; mean of 5 per-round deltas vs rep on CPU part 0xd40). rep2, a byte-identical REPORT-only function in the same rounds, is the null; arm-rep and rep2-rep share each round's rep, so inference uses the paired per-round difference arm-rep2 with an exact two-sided sign-flip test. With 5 pairs the smallest attainable p is 0.0625, so NO profiler cost is statistically established at alpha 0.05 (an earlier unpaired 5-vs-5 test reported p=0.008; withdrawn). Estimates with a consistent direction (all 5 paired differences one sign and every round beyond the null's largest |delta|; descriptive, p=0.0625): cProfile +113 ms Init (14%); Telemetry extension +93 ms Init (11%); py-spy +4.7% median per warm request; lkaisamp +457 ms cold first-request Duration. Phase timers and X-Ray show no consistent direction on any phase (null spread up to 28 ms Init, 155 ms cold Duration, 112 ms Restore Duration, 35 ms first restored request, ~1.8% warm); not proof of zero cost. lkaisamp's first-after-restore Duration rose +1.5 to +1.8 s in 3 of 5 rounds but not in 2 (p=0.25); the delta is outside the baseline's internal timing but before lkai_prof.handler returns, and attribution within its dump/symbolise hook remains open. Final latency comparisons should use REPORT or phase timers only. Host variability (results.json -> host_variability, reanalysis of committed evidence, no new spend): three CPU part IDs served the run (0xd40 4,225 rows, 0xd0c 528, 0xd4f 47), in every arm; no generation is inferred from them. Each loaded its own ggml CPU variant (0xd40 armv8.6_1, 0xd0c armv8.2_2, 0xd4f armv8.6_2), so kernels differ by part. No log stream changed part ID (4,472 of 4,800 rows linked). Unknown: per-invocation implementer/variant/revision/features, HWCAPs, core count and restored core count, cgroup limits, per-invocation kernel, AZ, snapshot-build host. Overhead cells are 0xd40-only, so the part mix cannot move them; pooled figures depend on the mix (rep warm REPORT p50 650 ms on 0xd40 vs 1,188 ms on 0xd0c). Hot spots (shares of all recorded samples): cold = S3 download 25.0 s (69.4%; 58% of py-spy init samples in TLS read) then the KleidiAI repack 8.4 s (23.3%; buffer_set_tensor 30.8% + rhs_pack 12.2% of init CPU samples pooled over parts; buffer_set_tensor 26.4% on 0xd40, 37.6% on 0xd0c, 30.3% on 0xd4f; single-threaded offline). Restore = Lambda restore 3.21 s (82%), then a first forward 2.8x warm whose CPU samples are 51% memset inside llama_kv_cache::clear / llama_memory_recurrent::clear (0xd40). Warm (0xd40) = KleidiAI i8mm matmul 49% of CPU, then f32 dot 9%, gated-delta-net 8%, concat 6%, OpenMP barrier 5%, fwht 5%. Warm concat is 5.6% in Lambda vs 2.65% offline under the same sampler on the same part ID 0xd40; not attributed to code (unrecorded host factors). Run 20261020T124451Z is superseded: one pooled Lambda client across SnapStart waits lost 45 restore invokes to client timeouts (this was earlier misreported as a Lambda platform stall), and its noise floor was the X-Ray arm itself. Status is inconclusive because this is a measurement study, not a latency change.
